title: First music remembered, phonograph cylinders, father as violinist
summary: Asked about his first music, Brunies talks of his father's cylinder phonograph, learning new pieces by ear, and his father playing violin by ear.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I was going to ask about other music. The very first music you remember hearing when you were a boy. Do you remember what kind of music? Did you hear any music down at the river? Or was it parades? Or your father playing? Or what was the first music?
I imagine you copied plenty of that off those folks. Oh, parades.

Like my daddy used to have a big phonograph, you know. It was a cylinder ring. Oh, yes. And we had a bar on my people. Yeah, bar on the confectionery. And I used to have my trumpet underneath the ball all the time. New piece come out, I put it on, I line it. And I played that day, that night at a ball or a picnic, I got the rest of the fellas to play it. And the whole band of players, I know people. I used to say, how are you learning pieces so quick? I said, it comes through my head.
It's nice to have this. We remember it all the time. We had this on the record.
You remember them all the time.

You were going to talk about your father a little bit being a fine violin player. Oh, yeah. He was a nice father. Not fine music. Just all my ear. Yes. Did he ever have any lessons, do you think? Or did his father help him? Where did he learn it? Did he ever say? I don't know. He just picked it up. He just picked it up. He just picked it up. He just picked it up. He just picked it up. He just picked it up. Yep. Where was your house where you lived? Jackson Avenue, Chapel Tula.
